# EQ6-R Pro ~136 s RA Tracking Spike

Last revised: 2026-10-20

Citation-backed investigation of a fast ~7" RA spike recurring every 134–138 s on a
Sky-Watcher EQ6-R Pro that has already had all bearings and belts replaced.

**Full deliverable:** [analysis.md](analysis.md) ·
**Per-dimension detail:** [references/](references/) ·
**Sources:** [citations.md](citations.md) · **Verification:** [audit/](audit/) ·
**Run report:** [report.md](report.md)

## Summary

No stock gear, pulley or belt in the EQ6-R RA drive turns at 134–138 s. The motor pulley is
119.7 s, the worm 478.7 s, and the 71-tooth belt 708.1 s (est., from the 180:1 + 48:12 spec
[1]). The one rotating part found in range is a **608 bearing on the worm shaft**: a damaged
or non-standard ball produces a line at 136.2–142.3 s (est., from 608 geometry [9][10] and
bearing-defect formulas [11]). The one solved EQ6-family case at this period matches. A
legacy EQ6 had a **133 s spike caused by "upgraded" ceramic worm bearings**, fixed by
refitting original 608s, back to 0.4" RMS [15]. An Exos2-GT with an almost identical ~134 s,
5–9" spike went away after belt re-tensioning, removal of worm-shaft play and other setup changes, cause not isolated [16]. An EQ6-R
Pro with 133 s/67 s harmonics stayed unresolved after a motor swap [18].

## Key periods

| Element | Period | Matches 134–138 s? |
|---|---|---|
| Worm | 478.7 s [15] | No |
| Motor pulley (12T) | 119.7 s (est.) | No; this is where pulley faults show [20][22] |
| Belt tooth mesh | 9.97 s (est.) | No |
| 71T belt: revolution / 5th harmonic / beat with motor | 708.1 / 141.6 / 144.0 s (est.) | No |
| 608 worm bearing, inner race | 107.7–110.4 s (est.) | No |
| **608 worm bearing, ball defect (2 × BSF)** | **136.2–142.3 s (est.)** | **Low end overlaps** |

## Decision steps

1. **Pin the period.** Record unguided for ~40 min with mount guide output off, then analyse
   in PECPrep [36][38]. Guiding and FFT bins both shift the apparent period [15][36].
2. **Read the result.** ~120 s points to the motor pulley or shaft [20][22]. ~10 s points to
   the belt teeth [26]. ~136.2–142.3 s, non-harmonic, is consistent with a worm-bearing ball
   defect (est.).
3. **Check the worm 608s you fitted.** Note brand, shield type (2Z vs 2RS [29]), and ceramic
   or 4-ball variants [13][14]. If they're non-standard or ceramic, try standard steel 608 2Z
   first. That is the fix in [15].
4. **Check assembly.** Worm end float "just over finger tight" [25]. Belt slack 4–5 mm
   (Sky-Watcher via [21]). Back off the worm mesh if you can hear a tone change during slow
   slews [28].
5. **Skip** a motor replacement [18], firmware [17], and PEC [38]. None removed a spike like
   this.

## Caveats

- No solved case on an EQ6-R Pro itself. The two solved cases are a legacy EQ6 and an
  Exos2-GT.
- The bearing-period link is this document's own calculation. No astronomy source reports
  it.
- Search used one web engine (Yahoo). Forum pages were supplied by the operator.
